Start Claude Code with --chrome so the Claude in Chrome MCP server comes up. Applies to every Claude session (from the next turn) and needs the Chrome extension; reviews only get it when MCP is allowed below.

Off by default: the review family (review / re-review / recheck / automation) connects no MCP server and only reads the repository. On, reviews connect every MCP server configured in your CLI, like sessions do — including tools that write to external systems, and automatic reviews run unattended. Shared by both providers. Servers declared inside the PR branch itself (.mcp.json / .codex/config.toml) are never enabled for a review.

Precision only counts reviews a human handled (ticked or posted) — a draft nobody looked at says nothing about the skill and is left out; rechecks and automation are counted from their own records.

Precision = human-accepted (ticked or posted) ÷ all findings; machine ticks (auto / engine) do not count as accepted. Cost per accepted = every run of those reviews ÷ accepted findings — what one useful finding costs.
